patch.objective: Apply a restrictive transfusion threshold and monitor a transfusion closely from the start, stopping at once for a suspected reaction
secondaryObjectives: Administer medications safely, including IV therapy, and recognize interactions and adverse reactions

sources.cite: MSNCB, 2023 CMSRN Exam Blueprint: Patient/Care Management (32%)
sources.note: Relayed from the CMSRN course seed (backend/supabase/seed/tracks/cmsrn.ts), which read the blueprint 2026-11-14, not re-read for this band. Patient/Care Management covers the nursing process, safety, medication and pre- and post-procedure care. Scope only.
The objective and secondary objectives are the course's own titles.

sources.cite: Australian Red Cross Lifeblood. Management of suspected reactions (clinical practice guidance)
sources.note: Relayed from the NCLEX-RN case post-op-transfusion-reaction, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-11: 'Stop the transfusion immediately and activate emergency procedures if required'; check ABC and vital signs; 'Maintain intravenous (IV) access (do not flush the existing line and use a new IV line if required)'; 'Repeat all clerical and identity checks'; 'Notify your Medical Officer and Transfusion Service Provider'; send fresh blood and urine samples with the used pack and IV line if asked; document and report; dyspnea or hypotension reactions 'Within 15 minutes of starting transfusion but may be later'; for suspected acute hemolysis maintain blood pressure and urine output.

Relayed from the NCLEX-RN case post-op-transfusion-reaction, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-11: fever and chills 'can also be the first sign of a more serious acute hemolytic reaction'; hypotension and red urine (hemoglobinuria) point to a more serious reaction; complications include DIC and renal failure; when a reaction is suspected 'the transfusion should be immediately stopped' with the line kept open with 0.9% saline; vital signs 'typically recorded at 15-minute intervals'.
